exemptCapabilities.reason: No pinned reference linter has a rule that reads callees transitively, which is what Rerail's calls capability answers.
exemptCapabilities.evidence: Checked Ruff 0.16.9 and Bandit 1.9.4. Ruff's rules that look at a call read only the call itself or the direct callee: flake8-async's ASYNC2xx and flake8-bugbear's call rules match the callee's resolved name; RET503 (crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/flake8_return/rules/function.rs, is_noreturn_func) reads only the direct callee's own `def` in the same file for a `NoReturn` annotation; Pyflakes' rules read bindings, not callees. Bandit's call tests (B3xx, B6xx, B113, B505) match the callee's qualified name through its import. None answers whether a function reaches a call of X through any chain of calls.
coveredBy: T2: fixtures/python/calls (calls::python_tests::python_calls_agree_with_the_runtime, against CPython 3.13.14 runtime traces)

suppressionExemptions.reason: Ruff never lets a noqa comment silence PGH004, which reports the noqa comments themselves: crates/ruff_linter/src/checkers/noqa.rs:65 skips PGH004 when it applies noqa directives, and only a file-level directive that names it (noqa.rs:273) turns it off, which the document matches.
